neighbours.label: a word stem split off before an '-ion(s)' suffix, predicting the -ion ending (dark complex|ions, the process|ions, four access|ions)
fire: Portraits of the era favoured sitters with pale complexions and dark hair.
Every Easter the town fills with religious processions through the old streets.
The library catalogues its new accessions every month.
The kingdom suffered several disputed successions after the king died.
Sun damage had left both sailors with ruddy, weathered complexions.
Torchlit processions wound up the hill to the cathedral.
The archive received two large accessions of letters last year.
Medieval law tried to settle royal successions without bloodshed.
quiet: Portraits of the era favoured complex compositions and dark backgrounds.
Every Easter the town repeats the same process of cleaning the old streets.
The library lets members access its new books every month.
The kingdom enjoyed great success in trade after the king died.
Sun damage had left both sailors with a complex mix of scars.
The process of building the cathedral took centuries.
The archive gives free access to letters from last year.
Medieval law had little success in preventing bloodshed.

notes: Output promotes 'ion', 'ions', 'ioned'. Fire uses plural -ions forms (split by the tokenizer); near misses use the same stem as a whole word.
